title: NCLEX 5,000 source import audit
method: Exact deduplication by normalized question stem, ordered option text/correctness, and rationale. One canonical record retained per identical item; all source IDs preserved.

groups.questionStem: A nurse is performing an assessment on a client diagnosed with Chronic Kidney Disease scheduled to receive Lisinopril. Which finding is the highest priority for the nurse to follow up?

options.text: New onset of confusion and dizziness upon standing.
Mild fatigue reported during morning activities.
Heart rate of 74 beats per minute.
Normal bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants.

groups.rationale: New onset altered mental status and orthostatic symptoms pose an immediate safety risk (fall risk and cerebral hypoperfusion) in a client with Chronic Kidney Disease taking Lisinopril.

groups.questionStem: A nurse is caring for a client with Sepsis who is prescribed Warfarin. Which clinical indicators require immediate intervention by the nurse? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client reports sudden onset of acute dyspnea and blood-tinged sputum.
Serum electrolyte panel reveals a potassium level of 2.8 mEq/L.
Blood pressure reading of 122/78 mmHg.
Urine output decreased to 15 mL/hr over the past 2 hours.
Capillary blood glucose level of 110 mg/dL.

groups.rationale: Severe hypokalemia, acute dyspnea, and oliguria (<30 mL/hr) indicate critical deterioration in a client with Sepsis receiving Warfarin and require immediate intervention.
